acceptance.given: The six materially distinct Matrix Cases are enumerated and their execution plans, fixture inputs, and state seeds are available for inspection.

oracle.expected: A validation run records six Matrix Case executions and proves that each case uses a distinct fixture identity and distinct execution-state assignment; the evidence maps every case to its own fixture/state pair and shows no pair is reused across materially distinct cases.
forbidden: Any two materially distinct Matrix Cases share a fixture identity or indistinguishable execution state.
The validation only asserts that six cases ran without proving fixture and state distinctness.
Fixture or state is normalized or overwritten so that case distinctions disappear during execution.
oracle.observable: The generated Matrix Case execution evidence contains six case-keyed records with pairwise-distinct fixture and state identifiers, plus a validation result showing the pairwise-distinctness check passed.

acceptance.then: The fixture/state distinctness validation passes for all six cases.
acceptance.when: After preparing and executing all six materially distinct Matrix Cases, during the evaluation phase when execution evidence is reconciled.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select the six-case fixture/state distinctness assertion and fail when any two case records have the same fixture identity or indistinguishable state.
Select the execution evidence manifest and fail when one or more of the six required Matrix Case records is missing or cannot be attributed to a fixture/state pair.

affected_subjects: Fixture and state distinctness for Matrix Case executions
slice_hint.behavior_change: Require the Toolchain Matrix Case evidence validator to preserve and verify a unique fixture identity and execution-state assignment for each of the six materially distinct cases, with pairwise-distinctness recorded as an evaluated structural result.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing case-evidence fields and validation behavior; only add the required six-case distinctness proof and reject ambiguous or reused fixture/state assignments.

slice_hint.state_transition: From six materially distinct cases lacking proven fixture/state separation to six executed, case-keyed records whose fixture and state assignments are pairwise distinct and attributable.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The validator emits a successful six-case distinctness result only when all six case records exist and every fixture/state pair is unique; otherwise it fails closed with the offending case keys.

acceptance.given: An external process is launched through the Toolchain process execution path with a configured finite time budget.

oracle.expected: The process execution record contains a positive finite timeout, and the process either completes or is terminated by that timeout before the budget expires; the terminal record is deterministic and marks timeout termination as unsuccessful.
forbidden: The external process is launched without a finite timeout.
The process remains running after the configured time budget.
Budget exhaustion is reported as success or leaves no deterministic terminal state.
The check only inspects a configuration value without observing process completion or termination.
oracle.observable: A process execution evidence record shows the configured finite deadline, an observed completion or timeout termination timestamp within that deadline, and a terminal status consistent with completion or unsuccessful timeout.

acceptance.then: The bounded process execution has a deterministic terminal outcome within its finite time bound.
acceptance.when: During external process execution, at the runtime evaluation phase after the process exits or the timeout handler terminates it.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select an external-process run with no observed completion or timeout termination before its configured finite deadline and fail the bounded-execution assertion.
Select a process invocation whose timeout is absent, non-finite, non-positive, or whose budget-exhausted terminal status is incorrectly successful.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Constrain every Toolchain external-process invocation to a positive finite timeout and record deterministic completion or timeout termination, treating budget exhaustion as unsuccessful.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Keep existing process result and runtime-evidence fields compatible; add or enforce finite timeout and deterministic timeout terminal semantics without changing caller contracts.

slice_hint.state_transition: From an executing external process with a time budget to a recorded completed or timeout-terminated process, with timeout termination classified unsuccessful.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Every invocation has a positive finite timeout and produces a terminal evidence record before the deadline; a timeout produces failure, never success.

acceptance.given: A replay result has an unexplained change in an input that determines the result, and the replay validator can compare the recorded binding inputs with the current inputs.

oracle.expected: The replay validator detects the unexplained result-determining input drift and either marks the result stale or terminates replay through a fail-closed outcome; no current or valid verdict is emitted.
forbidden: The result remains treated as current or valid despite unexplained result-determining input drift.
Replay proceeds as valid without stale classification or fail-closed termination.
The validator silently refreshes or ignores the drift and emits an otherwise successful verdict.
oracle.observable: The replay result contains a stale classification or a fail-closed terminal status, with evidence identifying the result-determining input drift and the decision that prevented a valid replay verdict.

acceptance.then: The replay is stale or has failed closed, and no valid current result is published.
acceptance.when: After binding comparison detects unexplained drift, during the semantic replay evaluation phase before any verdict is accepted or published.

failure_intents.selector_intent: Select the replay drift decision assertion and fail when unexplained result-determining input drift does not produce stale classification or fail-closed termination.
Select the replay evidence record and fail when it lacks attributable drift details, a stale/fail-closed terminal status, or proof that no valid verdict was published.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Make Toolchain replay validation compare result-determining inputs and fail closed on unexplained drift by emitting an explicit stale classification or terminal failure with attributable evidence and suppressing a valid verdict.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Retain existing replay result schema and valid-result behavior when inputs are unchanged; add explicit stale/fail-closed states for unexplained result-determining drift.

slice_hint.state_transition: From a replay with unexplained result-determining input drift and no accepted disposition to a stale result or fail-closed replay terminal state that cannot publish a valid current verdict.
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The validator records the detected drift and emits stale or fail-closed status before verdict publication; any current/valid result under unexplained drift is rejected.
